drivingQuestion: Why derive from 'in it' that he may not dwell in the boundary?
outcomeNote: Rav Sheshet finds a case the derivation is needed for

segments.he: ״לָדוּר״? תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּאֵין עוֹשִׂין שָׂדֶה מִגְרָשׁ וְלֹא מִגְרָשׁ שָׂדֶה, לֹא מִגְרָשׁ עִיר וְלֹא עִיר מִגְרָשׁ. אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לִמְחִילּוֹת.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Why is it necessary to state that the murderer may not «dwell» on the outskirts of the city? «Let him derive» that halakha from the fact «that one may not render the field» of a Levite city «an open space, nor an open space a field, nor an open space» part of the «city, nor» the «city an open space.» Apparently, the outskirts of the city, whose status is that of an open space, may not be utilized for residential purposes. «Rav Sheshet said: It is necessary» to state this halakha «only for tunnels.» If a murderer excavated a tunnel on the outskirts of the city, although he did not violate the prohibition against ruining the fields of the city, he may not reside there based on the halakha by Torah law that he must reside inside the city.

moves.summary: the prohibition on converting open land already forbids dwelling there
moves.about: why derive that he may not dwell in the boundary when converting open land to city is anyway forbidden

moves.cueHe: אמר רב ששת: לא נצרכה אלא למחילות
moves.summary: needed for tunnels dug under the open land
moves.about: the derivation is needed only for tunnels, which do not alter the open land
